methodology: The study utilized tensile tests and Izod impact tests on epoxy composites reinforced with kenaf fibers at different loading levels (10%, 20%, and 30 vol%). Scanning electron microscopy was employed to analyze the fracture morphology under both tensile and dynamic conditions.
research_objective: To investigate and report for the first time the tensile and dynamic impact toughness of epoxy composites reinforced with kenaf fibers, providing insights into their potential as sustainable alternatives to synthetic fiber composites.

key_findings.finding: Epoxy composites reinforced with kenaf fibers exhibit significantly higher tensile and impact toughness compared to neat epoxy, with values exceeding those of the corresponding dynamic impact toughness.
The tensile toughness of epoxy composites ranges from 9.36 kJ/m² at 10 vol% fiber content to 52.30 kJ/m² at 30 vol% fiber content, representing a three-to-one increase.
Investigation of tensile and dynamic (Izod impact) toughness in epoxy composites reinforced with kenaf fibers
Establishment of a comprehensive understanding of kenaf fiber reinforcement in epoxy matrices for future structural applications
Fiber orientation was consistent across specimens, as indicated by the reproducibility of mechanical results.
The average fiber density in the composites is 1.53 g/cm³, while the epoxy resin density is reported as 1.11 g/cm³.

The approach of recording stress-strain curves directly from the testing machine without compliance correction was justified due to the relatively large specimen dimensions compared to the machine stiffness.
All groups were tested under identical conditions, preserving the validity of comparisons between neat epoxy and kenaf fiber composites.
